Al-Zajjaj said: He made the whip with which He struck them to be the punishment.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means that He sees, hears and perceives everything.

Al-Kalbi said: He is upon the path of the servants, and none of them escapes Him. Muqatil said: the people pass by Him, and al-Mirsad (the place of observation) and al-Marsad mean the path.

﴿On that Day, none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds.﴾ Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read "yu'adhdhabu" and "yuwthaqa" with a fatha on the dhal and the tha', meaning: none [in the world] will be punished like the punishment of God on that Day, and none will be bound like His binding on that Day. [The word "fi al-dunya" (in the world) is omitted in manuscript A.] [The word "ahad" (anyone) is omitted in manuscript B.]

It was also said that this refers to a specific man, Umayya ibn Khalaf, meaning that none will be punished like the punishment of this disbeliever, and none will be bound like his binding.

The others read with a kasra on the dhal and the tha', i.e., none will punish in the world like God punishes the disbeliever on that Day, and none will bind like His binding. That is, no creature will reach the level of God's severity in punishment. "Al-wathaq" means being held in chains and shackles.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O soul at peace﴾ [i.e., "at peace" with] what God, Mighty and Majestic, has promised, the one who affirms what God has said. Mujahid said: "al-Mutma'innah" is the one who is certain that God, Exalted is He, is her Lord, and who is steadfast in heart toward His command and obedience.

Al-Hasan said: the believer who is certain. 'Atiyyah said: the one content with the decree of God, Exalted is He. Al-Kalbi said: the one secure from the punishment of God.

It was also said: the one reassured by the remembrance of God, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and their hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾.

They differed about the time of this address. A group said: it is said to her at the time of death, and it is said to her: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, i.e., to God, ﴿well-pleased﴾ with the reward, ﴿and well-pleasing [to Him]﴾, [pleasing] to Him toward you.

Al-Hasan said: when God wills to take her, she is at rest in God, content with God, and God is content with her.

Abdullah ibn Amr said: [In manuscript A it is written "Umar," which is an error.] When the believing servant dies, God, Mighty and Majestic, sends two angels to him, and sends to him a gift from Paradise. Then it is said to her: "Come out, O soul at peace; come out to comfort and fragrant plants, and your Lord is pleased with you." So she comes out like the finest scent of musk that anyone has ever smelled in his nose. The angels upon the horizons of the heaven say: "A good spirit has come from the earth, and a good breath." She does not pass by any gate without it being opened for her, nor by any angel without him sending blessings upon her, until she is brought before the Merciful, and she prostrates. Then it is said to Mika'il: "Take her and place her with the souls of the believers." Then he is commanded, and his grave is widened for him, seventy cubits in width and seventy cubits in length, and fragrant plants are scattered for him in it. If he had anything of the Qur'an with him, its light suffices him. If not, a light like the sun is placed for him in his grave, and he is like a bride, who sleeps and is not awakened except by the dearest of his family to him.

When the disbeliever dies, God sends to him two angels and sends a piece of coarse cloth, more foul than any stench and rougher than any roughness. It is said: "O soul that is evil, come out to Hell and painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you." [This is a fragment from the statement (mawquf) of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, recorded by Abd al-Razzaq in "al-Musannaf" 3/564–566, and Hannad in "al-Zuhd" 1/252–253. Al-Haythami said (2/328): "Al-Tabarani narrated it in 'al-Kabir' and its narrators are trustworthy." Al-Suyuti attributed it to Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd in "al-Tafsir," and al-Tabarani in "al-Kabir" with a chain whose narrators are trustworthy. See: "Sharh al-Sudur bi-Sharh Hal al-Mawta wa al-Qubur," p. 88, where Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani appears, who is weak; he has an entry in "al-Mizan" and "al-Tahdhib."]

Abu Salih said regarding His saying: "Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing": He said: this is at the moment of her departure from the world. Then, when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: "Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise."

Others said: this is only said to her at the Resurrection. It is said: "Return [to your Lord]" [Omitted in manuscript A], i.e., to your companion and your body, so God commands the spirits to return to the bodies. This is the view of Ikrimah, Ata', and al-Dahhak, and a narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: return to the reward of your Lord and His honor, well-pleased with God for what He has prepared for you, and well-pleasing [to Him], your Lord is pleased with you.

﴿So enter among My servants﴾, that is, along with My servants into My Paradise. It is also said: among the whole company of My righteous, obedient, and chosen servants. A parallel to this is: "And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants."

**[Commentary of al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 89, verse 30]**

﴿And enter My Paradise.﴾ Some of the people of *ishara* (*ahl al-ishara*, the Sufi interpreters who draw allusive, inward meanings from the text) said: "O soul at peace with the world, return to God by abandoning it. And returning to God is taking the path of the Hereafter."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, died in al-Ta'if, and I attended his funeral. A bird came, in the form of one of God's creatures, which we did not see [in "ب": lam yar], and it entered his bier. Then we did not see [in "ب": lam yar] it come out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, and we did not know who recited it: "O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. So enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise." [Al-Suyuti attributed this to Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani in *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 8/515.]
